fruits.extendedStory: The tale goes on that Hamburg searched his ship and found no treasure, so a carpenter bought it to break up. It is said his saw hit something hard and shining. The masts, so the story goes, were full of gold, silver and copper. Inside waits a story that is simply true. Johann Sebastian Bach played this organ for two hours in 1720 and could not praise its sound enough.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Man erzählt, die Hamburger hätten sein Schiff vergeblich nach Schätzen durchsucht und es einem Zimmermann zum Zerlegen verkauft. Der Sage nach traf seine Säge auf etwas Hartes, Schimmerndes, und die Masten waren voller Gold, Silber und Kupfer. Drinnen wartet eine Geschichte, die einfach wahr ist. Johann Sebastian Bach spielte 1720 zwei Stunden lang auf dieser Orgel und konnte ihren Klang nicht genug rühmen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The tale goes on that Hamburg searched his ship and found no treasure, so a carpenter bought it to break up. It is said his saw hit something hard and shining. The masts, so the story goes, were full of gold, silver and copper. Inside waits a story that is simply true. Johann Sebastian Bach played this organ for two hours in 1720 and could not praise its sound enough.

localizedStory.de: Schau hinauf zur Krone am Turm. Der Legende nach stammt ihr Gold aus dem Schatz des Piraten Klaus Störtebeker.
localizedStory.en: Look up at the crown on the tower. Legend has it its gold came from the treasure of the pirate Klaus Störtebeker.

fruits.name: Hauptkirche St. Katharinen
fruits.story: Look up at the crown on the tower. Legend has it its gold came from the treasure of the pirate Klaus Störtebeker.

fruits.extendedStory: Inside stands the organ Arp Schnitger finished in 1693. In 1919 it was run down and about to be replaced. Then the writer Hans Henny Jahnn and a friend came across it on a walk. They wrote to the church council at once, and Jahnn won the right to restore it. In the war its pipes were taken out and stored, so they survived when the church was wrecked. The church's second organ has a stop with a funny name, Wooden Laughter, a xylophone out of a cinema organ.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Drinnen steht die Orgel, die Arp Schnitger 1693 fertigstellte. 1919 war sie heruntergekommen und sollte ersetzt werden. Da stießen der Schriftsteller Hans Henny Jahnn und ein Freund bei einem Spaziergang auf sie. Die beiden schrieben sofort an den Kirchenrat, und Jahnn bekam die Erlaubnis, sie zu restaurieren. Im Krieg lagerte man die Pfeifen aus, so überstanden sie die Zerstörung. Die zweite Orgel hat ein Register mit lustigem Namen, Hölzern Gelächter, ein Xylophon aus einer Kino-Orgel.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Inside stands the organ Arp Schnitger finished in 1693. In 1919 it was run down and about to be replaced. Then the writer Hans Henny Jahnn and a friend came across it on a walk. They wrote to the church council at once, and Jahnn won the right to restore it. In the war its pipes were taken out and stored, so they survived when the church was wrecked. The church's second organ has a stop with a funny name, Wooden Laughter, a xylophone out of a cinema organ.

localizedStory.de: Pilger holen sich hier bis heute ihren Stempel. Einst war dies eine Kapelle für Pilger auf dem Weg zum Grab des Jakobus in Santiago.
localizedStory.en: Pilgrims still collect their stamp at the counter here. Long ago this was a little chapel for pilgrims walking to St James's grave in Santiago.

fruits.name: Evangelisch-lutherische Hauptkirche St. Jacobi
fruits.story: Pilgrims still collect their stamp at the counter here. Long ago this was a little chapel for pilgrims walking to St James's grave in Santiago.

fruits.extendedStory: The man who paid for it, Henry Sloman, had left for Chile without a penny and came home rich from Chilean saltpetre. A shipping firm called Rob. M. Sloman already had a Slomanhaus, so he named his after Chile. He wanted it shaped like a passenger ship and bought 4.8 million bricks for it. Its pointed tip looks like a ship's bow, and up there sits an Andean condor, Chile's bird. Even the street Fischertwiete runs right under the house.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Bezahlt hat das Haus Henry Sloman. Er war ohne einen Pfennig nach Chile gegangen und kam durch Salpeter reich zurück. Weil eine Reederei namens Rob. M. Sloman schon ein Slomanhaus hatte, nannte er seines Chilehaus. Es sollte aussehen wie ein Passagierschiff, und er kaufte dafür 4,8 Millionen Ziegel. Die Spitze erinnert an einen Schiffsbug, und oben sitzt ein Andenkondor, das Wappentier Chiles. Sogar die Fischertwiete läuft mitten unter dem Haus hindurch.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The man who paid for it, Henry Sloman, had left for Chile without a penny and came home rich from Chilean saltpetre. A shipping firm called Rob. M. Sloman already had a Slomanhaus, so he named his after Chile. He wanted it shaped like a passenger ship and bought 4.8 million bricks for it. Its pointed tip looks like a ship's bow, and up there sits an Andean condor, Chile's bird. Even the street Fischertwiete runs right under the house.

localizedStory.de: Angeblich wählte Fritz Höger hier Ausschussklinker, gut für Schweineställe, weil die Brocken zu seinem Riesenbau passten. Historiker zweifeln daran.
localizedStory.en: Fritz Höger told the tale that he chose lumpy reject bricks for these walls, fit for pigsties, because they suited his giant. Historians doubt it.

fruits.name: Chilehaus
fruits.story: Fritz Höger told the tale that he chose lumpy reject bricks for these walls, fit for pigsties, because they suited his giant. Historians doubt it.

fruits.extendedStory: Check the main door under the tower. Its left handle is a bronze lion's head, which the parish calls Hamburg's oldest work of art. The words around it record when the tower's foundation stone was laid, in 1342. High above, watchmen once kept guard at night. Every quarter of an hour one had to give a signal, so people knew he was awake. Their old room has a strange neighbour today: the emergency chaplains' little Smart car, lifted into the tower.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Schau dir die Haupttür unter dem Turm an. Ihr linker Türzieher ist ein bronzener Löwenkopf, laut Gemeinde das älteste Kunstwerk Hamburgs. Seine Umschrift hält fest, dass 1342 der Grundstein des Turms gelegt wurde. Hoch oben hielten früher Wächter nachts Wache. Alle Viertelstunde musste einer ein Signal geben, damit die Leute wussten: Der Wächter schläft nicht. Neben ihrer alten Stube steht heute ein seltsamer Nachbar, der kleine Smart der Notfallseelsorge, in den Turm gehoben.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Check the main door under the tower. Its left handle is a bronze lion's head, which the parish calls Hamburg's oldest work of art. The words around it record when the tower's foundation stone was laid, in 1342. High above, watchmen once kept guard at night. Every quarter of an hour one had to give a signal, so people knew he was awake. Their old room has a strange neighbour today: the emergency chaplains' little Smart car, lifted into the tower.

localizedStory.de: Niemand weiß sicher, wo die Kirche des Missionars Ansgar stand. Vieles deutet darauf hin, dass ihre Reste unter St. Petri liegen.
localizedStory.en: Nobody knows for sure where the missionary Ansgar's church stood. Much suggests its remains lie under St. Petri.

fruits.name: Hauptkirche St. Petri
fruits.story: Nobody knows for sure where the missionary Ansgar's church stood. Much suggests its remains lie under St. Petri.

fruits.extendedStory: After the fire, number 42 stuck out alone, as its neighbours were rebuilt further back to widen the street. The street's history says the fire began there. In the early 1970s these old houses nearly vanished, as the street was to become a through road. A journalist, Gisela Schiefler, and an architect, Gerhard Hirschfeld, fought for them, and the association Save the Deichstraße was founded. It held street lotteries, sold Deichstraße thalers and wrote begging letters, until it could buy a house of its own.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Nach dem Brand ragte Haus Nummer 42, wo er laut Straßenchronik ausbrach, einsam in die Straße. Die Nachbarn bauten weiter hinten neu, damit die Straße breiter wurde. Anfang der 1970er Jahre wären diese alten Häuser fast verschwunden, denn die Straße sollte eine Durchgangsstraße werden. Die Journalistin Gisela Schiefler und der Architekt Gerhard Hirschfeld kämpften für sie, und der Verein Rettet die Deichstraße wurde gegründet. Er veranstaltete Straßenlotterien, verkaufte Deichstraßentaler und schrieb unzählige Spendenbriefe, bis er ein eigenes Haus kaufen konnte.
localizedExtendedStory.en: After the fire, number 42 stuck out alone, as its neighbours were rebuilt further back to widen the street. The street's history says the fire began there. In the early 1970s these old houses nearly vanished, as the street was to become a through road. A journalist, Gisela Schiefler, and an architect, Gerhard Hirschfeld, fought for them, and the association Save the Deichstraße was founded. It held street lotteries, sold Deichstraße thalers and wrote begging letters, until it could buy a house of its own.

localizedStory.de: Man erzählt, im Mai 1842 erscholl hier der Ruf „Füer in de Diekstraat!“. Der Große Brand hatte begonnen, und niemand weiß genau, wie.
localizedStory.en: They say in May 1842 the cry 'Fire in the Deichstraße!' rang out here. The Great Fire had begun, and nobody knows exactly how.

fruits.name: Historische Häuser
fruits.story: They say in May 1842 the cry 'Fire in the Deichstraße!' rang out here. The Great Fire had begun, and nobody knows exactly how.

fruits.extendedStory: In 1857 a Laeisz ship was named Pudel after her, and that is how the poodle came to stand for the firm. Ship names beginning with P turned into a tradition the firm still keeps. Its tall ships are famous to this day as the Flying P-Line. Inside the house runs one of the few paternoster lifts still open to the public. It has no doors and keeps circling, a small challenge for anyone new to it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: 1857 bekam ein Schiff der Firma Laeisz ihr zu Ehren den Namen Pudel, und so wurde der Pudel zum Zeichen der Firma. Schiffsnamen mit P wurden zur Tradition, die die Firma bis heute pflegt. Ihre Großsegler sind weltweit als Flying P-Line berühmt. Im Haus fährt einer der wenigen Paternoster, die noch öffentlich zugänglich sind. Er hat keine Türen und fährt im Umlauf, eine kleine Herausforderung für jeden Neuling.
localizedExtendedStory.en: In 1857 a Laeisz ship was named Pudel after her, and that is how the poodle came to stand for the firm. Ship names beginning with P turned into a tradition the firm still keeps. Its tall ships are famous to this day as the Flying P-Line. Inside the house runs one of the few paternoster lifts still open to the public. It has no doors and keeps circling, a small challenge for anyone new to it.

localizedStory.de: Such an der Fleetseite den Bronzepudel auf dem Dach. Das Maskottchen geht auf Carl Laeisz’ Frau zurück, Spitzname Pudel, wegen ihrer krausen Haare.
localizedStory.en: Look for a bronze poodle on the roof's canal side. The firm's mascot honours Carl Laeisz's wife, nicknamed Pudel for her curly hair.

fruits.name: Laeiszhof
fruits.story: Look for a bronze poodle on the roof's canal side. The firm's mascot honours Carl Laeisz's wife, nicknamed Pudel for her curly hair.

fruits.extendedStory: That meadow castle stood right here. It was no stone fortress but a ring of earth and timber. The search for it almost became a myth, until archaeologists found it beyond doubt. The steel sculpture traces its old rampart, and the white seats mark the floor plan of the cathedral that came later. One bench has a little window onto an old pillar foundation. Its name lives on in Hamburg's big funfair, still called the DOM, the cathedral. That is because a Christmas market was once held inside it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Genau hier stand diese Wiesenburg. Sie war keine Steinfestung, sondern ein Wall aus Holz und Erde. Die Suche nach ihr wurde fast zum Mythos, bis Archäologen sie zweifelsfrei wiederentdeckten. Die Stahlskulptur zeichnet ihren Wall nach, und die weißen Sitzelemente markieren den Grundriss des späteren Mariendoms. In einer Bank schaust du durch ein Fenster auf den Rest eines Pfeilerfundaments. Sein Name lebt im großen Hamburger Volksfest weiter. Es heißt bis heute Dom, weil einst im Seitenschiff des Doms ein Weihnachtsmarkt stattfand.
localizedExtendedStory.en: That meadow castle stood right here. It was no stone fortress but a ring of earth and timber. The search for it almost became a myth, until archaeologists found it beyond doubt. The steel sculpture traces its old rampart, and the white seats mark the floor plan of the cathedral that came later. One bench has a little window onto an old pillar foundation. Its name lives on in Hamburg's big funfair, still called the DOM, the cathedral. That is because a Christmas market was once held inside it.

localizedStory.de: Der Sage nach verdankt Hamburg seinen Namen seinen guten Schinken. Tatsächlich hieß „ham“ eine umzäunte Wiese, die Hammaburg war also eine Wiesenburg.
localizedStory.en: The tale goes that Hamburg got its name from its fine smoked hams. Really, 'ham' meant a fenced meadow, so Hammaburg was the meadow castle.

fruits.name: Hammaburg-Platz
fruits.story: The tale goes that Hamburg got its name from its fine smoked hams. Really, 'ham' meant a fenced meadow, so Hammaburg was the meadow castle.

fruits.extendedStory: The old church had burned, and two thirds of Hamburg's households gave money for the new one. When its tower was finished in 1874, it was briefly the tallest building in the world. Badly damaged in the war, the church could have been rebuilt. But offices had replaced its parish's homes, and the congregation had largely gone. So all but the choir came down, and some stones went to shore up the Elbe bank. The ruin stays as a memorial against war.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die alte Kirche war abgebrannt, und zwei Drittel der Hamburger Haushalte spendeten für die neue. Als der Turm 1874 fertig war, war er für kurze Zeit das höchste Gebäude der Welt. Im Krieg schwer beschädigt, hätte die Kirche wieder aufgebaut werden können. Doch Bürohäuser hatten die Wohnungen verdrängt, und die Gemeinde war weitgehend fort. Also riss man die Mauern bis auf den Chor ab, und manche Steine befestigten danach das Elbufer. Die Ruine bleibt als Mahnmal gegen den Krieg.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The old church had burned, and two thirds of Hamburg's households gave money for the new one. When its tower was finished in 1874, it was briefly the tallest building in the world. Badly damaged in the war, the church could have been rebuilt. But offices had replaced its parish's homes, and the congregation had largely gone. So all but the choir came down, and some stones went to shore up the Elbe bank. The ruin stays as a memorial against war.

localizedStory.de: Gottfried Semper gewann den Wettbewerb für diese Kirche. Gebaut wurde der drittplatzierte gotische Entwurf, denn Gotik galt damals als deutscher Stil.
localizedStory.en: Gottfried Semper won the contest for this church. Hamburg built the third-placed Gothic design instead, because Gothic then counted as the German style.

fruits.name: Kirchenruine St. Nikolai
fruits.story: Gottfried Semper won the contest for this church. Hamburg built the third-placed Gothic design instead, because Gothic then counted as the German style.

fruits.extendedStory: In the courtyard stands the fountain of Hygieia, the goddess of health who gave hygiene its name. The plan had been Mercury, the god of trade, until a cholera epidemic changed the city's mind. Look at the arched openings in its base. They draw in the air for the rooms inside, cooled by the moving water. After the old town hall burned in 1842, the council made do with temporary rooms for 55 years.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Im Innenhof steht der Brunnen der Hygieia, der Göttin der Gesundheit, nach der die Hygiene heißt. Geplant war eigentlich Merkur, der Gott des Handels. Dann kam eine Choleraepidemie, und die Stadt entschied sich um. Schau auf die bogenförmigen Öffnungen im Sockel. Dort holt sich das Rathaus seine Luft, und das bewegte Wasser kühlt sie. Nach dem Brand des alten Rathauses 1842 tagte der Rat 55 Jahre lang in provisorischen Räumen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: In the courtyard stands the fountain of Hygieia, the goddess of health who gave hygiene its name. The plan had been Mercury, the god of trade, until a cholera epidemic changed the city's mind. Look at the arched openings in its base. They draw in the air for the rooms inside, cooled by the moving water. After the old town hall burned in 1842, the council made do with temporary rooms for 55 years.

localizedStory.de: Beim Festmahl für Ehrengäste wartet der Bürgermeister oben an der Treppe. Man sagt, so musste früher kein Bürgermeister Gästen vom Pferd helfen.
localizedStory.en: At its feast for guests of honour, the mayor waits atop the stairs. They say it spared old mayors helping riders dismount.

fruits.name: Rathaus
fruits.story: At its feast for guests of honour, the mayor waits atop the stairs. They say it spared old mayors helping riders dismount.

fruits.extendedStory: The part of the museum showing them got a nickname of its own, the chamber of horrors. The same director, Alfred Lichtwark, rediscovered the painter Caspar David Friedrich. Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog hangs here today, yet its famous title is not his. The unsigned picture got that name in 1950, after it turned up again, and it came to Hamburg in 1970. Citizens started it all. Mostly their donations paid for the museum's original home, on an old city bastion.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Derselbe Direktor, Alfred Lichtwark, entdeckte Caspar David Friedrich wieder und sicherte viele seiner Bilder für die Sammlung. Heute hängt hier sein Wanderer über dem Nebelmeer. Der berühmte Titel stammt aber nicht von Friedrich. Das unsignierte Bild bekam ihn erst 1950, nachdem es wiederentdeckt worden war, und kam 1970 nach Hamburg. Angefangen hat alles mit Hamburgs Bürgern. Vor allem ihre Spenden bezahlten das Museumshaus auf einer alten Bastion der Stadtbefestigung.

Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog hangs here today, yet its famous title is not his. The unsigned picture got that name in 1950, after it turned up again, and it came to Hamburg in 1970. Citizens started it all. Mostly their donations paid for the museum's original home, on an old city bastion.

localizedStory.de: Als der Direktor junge Maler Hamburg malen ließ, spotteten die Leute über Schmieralien und Spinat mit Ei. Die Abteilung bekam den Spitznamen Schreckenskammer.
localizedStory.en: When its director paid young painters to paint Hamburg, locals called the results smears and nicknamed them spinach with egg.

fruits.name: Hamburger Kunsthalle
